To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain is not an information processor, that it is not rational, and that it is not a computational device. Instead
the brain optimizes energy rather than information.
the human visual system optimizes the energy of the neural response rather than the information in the stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how cognitive systems minimize energy rather than information.
the development of a new class of cognitive models that are grounded in physical reality.
cognitive systems that are energy efficient and that can learn to be energy efficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“Cognitive systems optimize information, not energy.” This is a statement about cognitive systems, not about the human brain.
the brain is a cognitive system.
the brain optimizes the amount of energy it uses to process information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we should not focus on optimizing the information content of a process, but rather on optimizing its energy consumption.
cognitive systems optimize energy rather information.
cognitive systems optimize energy, not information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive models should focus on the physical constraints of the brain.
cognitive systems optimize energy rather then information.
the human cognitive system is an energy minimizer, and not an information minimizer.
